newsitem.title: UK: European PC sales projections slashed again.
newsitem.headline: European PC sales projections slashed again.

text.p: By Neil Winton, Science and Technology Correspondent

Personal computer sales growth in Europe is being hit by Germany's sluggish economic performance and targets for the year as a whole are being slashed again, according to a survey published on Monday.
Computer market researcher CONTEXT, in its third quarter review of the western European PC market, said it now expects growth for 1996 to slow to around 11.4 percent with 16.5 million machines sold.

This compares with industry forecasts of about 15 percent growth for the year back in August, and is less than half the 35 percent that industry forecaster Dataquest was extrapolating at the beginning of the year.
In 1995 European PC sales soared 35 percent.

In the latest quarter ended September 30, 1996, PC sales rose 8.3 percent to 3.4 million compared with the same period last year. First quarter growth was 13.2 percent, braking sharply to 8.1 percent in the second quarter, CONTEXT said.
Cumulative growth in the first three quarters was 10.1 percent.
"Most of the big European PC markets are suffering from the general economic recession that has hit consumer PC sales in Germany, Spain and Italy very badly," CONTEXT analyst Emmanuel Lalloz said.

"There is little chance of the Spanish and Italian markets picking up before the beginning of 1997 at the earliest. The future of the PC market looks uncertain in Germany too, since the recovery of the economy has not happened yet, contrary to what most analysts expected," Lalloz said.
Britain bucked the trend with sales up 19.6 percent in the quarter.
The survey showed that the top three corporate performers were all from the U.S.
COMPAQ Computer Corp, the world's biggest personal computer maker, easily retained its number one spot with a market share of 13.1 percent.
International Business Machines was second with 9.4 percent, which CONTEXT said was down to the price competitiveness of IBM's desktop products and the success of Thinkpad 365 mobile PCs.
Hewlett-Packard Co was third with 5.9 percent.
The first European was Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme with 5.1 percent.
CONTEXT said the best performance came from direct seller Dell Computer Corp. Its sales rose 49.1 percent, spearheaded by the Dell Dimension and Poweredge PCs.
Among the laggards, Apple Computer Inc lost just over one percentage point of market share, but CONTEXT saw some signs of recovery over the last two quarters.
The European PC market has seen vicious price competition this year. Prices are being slashed, or consumers are negotiating more computer power for the same money.
As profit margins are cut back, analysts wonder if all the competitors in the market can survive.
Already there has been one casualty. In July, German computer retailer Escom AG filed for bankruptcy as a result of this fierce price war.
